articles.description:
Across 591 scored skills, the weakest of our six evaluation dimensions is also the one that decides whether the skill gets used at all. The fix takes five minutes and almost nobody does it.
Your skill's description field is the only part of it that's loaded before the skill is chosen. The agent reads it, decides whether this skill matches the request, and only then loads the body. That makes it a routing table, not documentation.
We score it as "trigger quality," worth 20 of 100 points. Across 591 skills it averages 7.74 — the lowest of our six dimensions, behind content (8.30) and workflow design (8.11).
A description that scores well answers four questions:
What does it produce? — most skills do this.
When should it fire? — common, usually as Use when the user asks to ….

articles.description:
Imagine building an AI model to detect fraudulent transactions.
You train it on thousands of historical transactions. The results look incredible. It correctly classifies 99% of the training examples.
You deploy it, expecting it to catch fraud reliably.
But something goes wrong.
Legitimate transactions get flagged. New fraud patterns slip through. The model that looked almost perfect during training performs disappointingly on transactions it has never encountered before.
How can a model that performed so well suddenly become unreliable?
The problem might not be the model's architecture, its computing power, or even the quality of the training algorithm.
It might have learned the wrong things.
This is called overfitting, one of the fundamental problems in machine learning. It occurs when a…
